messages.author: 28ce76b0974e0e05
messages.subject: Shiny Server Open Sluggish on IE/Edge
parts: We are currently running Shiny Server Open (v 1.4.1.657) on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7.3 and an identical copy of this with Shiny Server Pro.  The open source version has long initial load times for applications when using Internet Explorer or Edge and will sometimes fail to load the application altogether.  These issues do not occur when using the Pro server with identical applications and configuration.  How do we configure Shiny Server Open to respond as quickly as the Pro version when using IE/Edge?

We are in the process of standing up another version of Shiny Server with the latest upgrade.  We should have results from that by tomorrow.  Maybe this issue will go away under the latest version.

That's quite surprising. Do you see any errors in the browser JavaScript console of either one?

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server Open Sluggish on IE/Edge
parts:
I don't know what TMG is either. :)

If you ever figure out what kind of proxy was slowing down Shiny Server Open Source without https, I'd love that data point. Thanks!
On Thu, Feb 2, 2017 at 11:20 AM Daniel Fealko <drfe...@gmail.com> wrote:

Bingo!  That appears to be it.  Our network guy ran the open version through the TMG (I don't understand this jargon) just like prod and now it too is fast.  We have to go through a thorough testing against this, but at least it looks promising.

Thanks so much for your quick help and guidance on this.  It's been driving us nuts for a while.


On Thursday, February 2, 2017 at 1:42:30 PM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
So the same errors on both, but production is still fast?

It could easily be https causing the difference if you have a proxy or two between your browser and server. Proxies tend to muck around with http requests (trying to be "helpful") much more than https.
On Thu, Feb 2, 2017 at 10:37 AM Daniel Fealko <drfe...@gmail.com> wrote:
An update: I do see the same websocket errors on the prod version too. 


On Thursday, February 2, 2017 at 12:28:09 PM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
You're sure there aren't different network or HTTP proxies between the two servers? Is one using http and the other https?
On Thu, Feb 2, 2017 at 9:21 AM Daniel Fealko <drfe...@gmail.com> wrote:
Correct, and Pro returns almost instantly.
